title: The 33-Level Axis
purpose: A navigational vertical scaffold for the atlas. It is a project architecture, not a claim that reality literally consists of 33 metaphysical layers.

orientation.horizontal_plane_rule: Every level may open onto a horizontal plane of records: entities, objects, places, institutions, events, systems, relationships and evidence.

bands.name: Orientation
bands.meaning: Direction, source, axis and the conditions for knowing where a record sits.

bands.name: Matter
bands.meaning: Physical substrate, objects, land, energy and built environments.

bands.name: Life
bands.meaning: Biology, ecology, bodies, growth, health and reproduction.

bands.name: Mind
bands.meaning: Perception, memory, knowledge, language, information and interpretation.

bands.name: People & Relations
bands.meaning: Persons, families, communities, peoples, migration and social relationships.

bands.name: Institutions
bands.meaning: Organizations, government, firms, schools, religions and durable coordination systems.

bands.name: Law & Civilization
bands.meaning: Law, property, rights, constitutions, culture, norms and historical civilization.

bands.name: Systems & History
bands.meaning: Economy, finance, energy, infrastructure, technology, trade, war and historical change.

bands.name: Meaning & Spirit
bands.meaning: Values, worldview, religion, symbolism, purpose and the project's interpretive layer.

levels.name: Meaning
levels.description: Questions of purpose, value and what a record means within a larger frame.

levels.name: Spirit & Worldview
levels.description: Religious, philosophical and spiritual systems that orient human interpretation.

levels.name: Systems
levels.description: Interacting economic, technological, infrastructural and political systems.

levels.name: History
levels.description: Events, sequences, inherited conditions, turning points and consequences.

levels.name: Strategic Relationships
levels.description: Dependencies, alliances, bottlenecks, obligations and major cross-system links.

levels.name: Civilization
levels.description: Large-scale patterns of institutions, culture, technology and collective organization.

levels.name: Law
levels.description: Formal rules, rights, duties, enforcement and legal institutions.

levels.name: Property & Control
levels.description: Ownership, control, land, assets, intellectual property and effective power.

levels.name: Constitution
levels.description: The distribution and limitation of political authority.

levels.name: Institutions
levels.description: Organizations that persist through time and coordinate people and resources.

levels.name: Government
levels.description: Public authorities, administration, budgets, regulation and state capacity.

levels.name: Economy Institutions
levels.description: Firms, banks, markets, funds and other organizations that coordinate production and capital.

levels.name: Social Institutions
levels.description: Schools, religious bodies, families, associations and cultural organizations.

levels.name: Relations
levels.description: Kinship, friendship, cooperation, conflict, exchange and other social ties.

levels.name: Communities
levels.description: People organized by place, language, belief, occupation, culture or shared identity.

levels.name: Peoples
levels.description: Ethnolinguistic, indigenous, national, diasporic and historical populations.

levels.name: Persons
levels.description: Individuals as actors with identities, biographies, roles and relationships.

levels.name: Mind
levels.description: Cognition, attention, perception, memory and interpretation.

levels.name: Knowledge
levels.description: Evidence, learning, science, expertise, archives and information systems.

levels.name: Language
levels.description: Systems through which people encode, transmit and negotiate meaning.

levels.name: Perception
levels.description: How observers encounter, classify and experience the world.

levels.name: Health & Reproduction
levels.description: Health, care, reproduction, development and biological continuity.

levels.name: Ecology
levels.description: Relationships among organisms, environments, resources and ecological processes.

levels.name: Bodies
levels.description: Human and non-human bodies as biological and social realities.

levels.name: Growth & Life
levels.description: Birth, growth, renewal, adaptation and the processes that sustain living systems.

levels.name: Built Environment
levels.description: Buildings, settlements and engineered environments.

levels.name: Infrastructure Matter
levels.description: Physical networks such as roads, rail, ports, grids, pipes and cables.

levels.name: Energy & Resources
levels.description: Energy, minerals, water, land and other material foundations of society.

levels.name: Objects & Land
levels.description: Physical things, territories and material assets that anchor records in space.

levels.name: Plane
levels.description: The horizontal field in which records exist together and relationships can be observed.

levels.name: Axis
levels.description: The vertical organizing principle that gives the planes a common orientation.

levels.name: Ladder
levels.description: The traversable sequence connecting levels without erasing their differences.

levels.name: North / Source
levels.description: The highest project orientation: source, direction, summit and the point from which the atlas is ordered.

epistemic_rule: Levels are an information architecture. A real-world record is not automatically more or less real because it is placed at a symbolic level. Evidence remains attached to the record itself.
